evals.prompt: Set up the storyboard for scene-03, a standard dialogue-and-reveal scene with one turn shot and two shots that use camera moves. No level has been chosen.
evals.expected_output: A board record at L2 with a recorded reason, start/peak/end panels on the turn shot and the moving shots, one panel on the other shots, and a passing check.
assertions: The level is L2 and the board records a reason for it.
The turn shot and each shot with a camera move get start, peak and end panels, and the remaining shots get one panel.
The panels copy size, angle, framing, move and light from the shot plan rather than inventing them.
The panel durations of each shot sum to the shot's duration in the plan.
The agent runs check and reports it passing before anything is generated.

evals.prompt: Scene-05 is a rooftop fight: three physical exchanges, a fall, and a reveal that depends on a prop breaking. Plan the storyboard level and panels.
evals.expected_output: A board at L3 with a recorded reason, sub-beat panels on the key shots, state changes carried in the plan, and a cost statement before generation.
assertions: The scene is set to L3 and the reason names the action, the fall or the prop change.
Key shots use sub-beats (anticipation, contact, consequence, reaction or the shot's own named beats) and non-key shots get one panel.
The prop break is carried as a state change so the board marks that shot key.
The agent states the panel count and the cost before any generation and does not generate yet.

evals.prompt: A quiet two-person dialogue scene with six held shots and a small budget. Plan its storyboard.
evals.expected_output: A board with a recorded level and reason that suits a quiet, held, budget-limited scene, and no more panels than that level needs.
assertions: The level is L1 with a recorded reason that cites the quiet held shots or the budget.
The board has one panel per shot, six in total.
The answer notes a single shot can later be raised with a recorded override.

evals.prompt: Review of scene-02's board found one panel (s02_sh010_p020) with a duplicated jar on the bench; the other eleven panels are approved. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: A repair plan that edits only that panel with seedream_edit_image under a one-dimension revision contract, keeps the other panels untouched, and lists only the affected sheet page and animatic segment as stale.
assertions: The panel is marked needs_edit and repaired by an image edit, not by regenerating the board or the shot.
The revision contract names one failed dimension, the requested change, acceptance criteria, and the locked decisions.
The edit uses HTTPS URLs from media_upload or media_presign and a bounding box for the local defect.
The result is registered as a new version of the same panel with the original kept as rejected.
The other eleven panels keep their files, hashes and approvals, and only the affected sheet page and animatic segment are rebuilt.

evals.prompt: The same panel failed again after two edits on the same dimension, and a second panel in another shot shows the wrong axis direction. What now?
evals.expected_output: Escalation: regenerate the first panel from a corrected prompt, regenerate the wrong-axis panel from a corrected prompt, and keep every other panel.
assertions: The twice-failed panel is regenerated from a corrected prompt instead of being edited a third time.
The wrong-axis panel is regenerated as a structural error rather than edited.
Neither repair regenerates the whole scene or the sibling panels, and the other panels stay untouched.

evals.prompt: Most panels of s04_sh020 (four panels, three failed) show the wrong boy because the element sheet bound to them was the old one. Repair the board.
evals.expected_output: Fix the element binding, then regenerate that shot's panels only, leaving other shots untouched.
assertions: The cause is treated as shared and the element binding is corrected first.
The shot's four panels are regenerated and the panels of other shots are not.
The new panels are registered as new takes or versions and the old files are kept as rejected.

evals.prompt: I changed the shot plan for scene-02 after the sheet and animatic were built. What do I need to redo, and can I feed the animatic to Seedance as a reference?
evals.expected_output: Check reports the board stale against the plan; status lists affected pages and segments; the animatic and sheet are never Seedance references.
assertions: The agent runs check and reports that the shot plan changed and the board is stale.
Only the sheet pages, overview and animatic segments that status lists are rebuilt.
The agent refuses to bind the animatic or any board file as a Seedance reference and says staging goes into the shot prompt text with element references only.

evals.prompt: I edited the shot plan of scene-02 after three panels were generated and registered. Update the board.
evals.expected_output: rebase-plan carries the registered panels over by id, marks panels whose plan facts changed as needs_edit, lists orphaned files, and does not use init --overwrite.
assertions: The agent uses rebase-plan and explains that init --overwrite is refused once panels are registered.
Registered files, versions and hashes survive the rebase for panels whose shot and state are unchanged.
A panel whose size, angle, framing or move changed in the plan is marked needs_edit and loses its approval.
Orphaned panel files are listed and left on disk rather than deleted.
